findings.text: _request_compilation_cache_key claims to describe static compiled-program inputs but omits request.clip_mode. The request path applies clip_mode through active.operator.with_clip_mode before solving, and clip mode selects distinct static support/moment branches. The independent cache-key probe constructs otherwise identical chord and exact requests and prints KEYS_EQUAL True before exiting 1. Once the chord key is stored, an exact request can set receipt.compilation_cache_hit true even though its clip-specific program has not been observed. Add request.clip_mode (or an identity that includes it) to the key and add a regression that asserts distinct modes have distinct keys and first-use cache misses.

The only new regression replaces profile._request_compilation_cache_key with lambda request, _initial_flux: request.clip_mode. That makes the tested key discriminator correct by construction and masks the production omission at forward.py:2690-2726. Exercise the real key (with a lightweight program-identity fixture if needed) and assert chord versus exact or chord_cells keys differ; then verify cache-hit provenance is false on each first mode and true only on a repeated same-mode request.

The first independent head-gate attempt exited 2 during collection because Numba attempted to create a cache beside read-only reviewed source. The rerun with NUMBA_DISABLE_JIT=1 completed 1 passed, EXIT=0. This is a review-environment constraint rather than a reviewed-code failure.

follow_ons: Repair ForwardProfile._request_compilation_cache_key so clip_mode participates in the key, or make ForwardFluxOperator.program_identity incorporate its request-owned clip mode.
